1022
Visual-induced startle reactions in a patient with stiff limb
syndrome
P. Schestatsky, A. Dall Pizzol, L. Cabral, A.S. Schuh, M. Roriz-Cruz,
F. Batistela, T.L. Monte, M.M. Bianchin, C.R.M. Rieder
(Porto Alegre, Brazil)
Objective: To report visual-induced startle reactions in a patient
with stiff limb syndrome.
Background: The stiff limb syndrome (SLS) is a rare condition
characterized by focal muscle stiffness, painful reﬂex spasms and
continuous motor unit activity as well as abnormal exteroceptive
reﬂexes. One of the most fascinating ﬁndings of SLS patients is the
reﬂex muscle spasm triggered by acoustic or tactile stimulation.
Methods: We report the case of a 74 year old woman with pro-
gressive stiffness of left leg that was not attributed to any known
structural lesion. We performed a full clinical, laboratory and neuro-
physiological investigation in order to exclude other causes of leg
stiffness.
Results: MRI of the brain and entire spinal cord, as well as gen-
eral laboratory ﬁndings were unremarkable, including serum glutamic
acid decarboxilase antibodies levels and cerebrospinal ﬂuid parame-
ters. However, during the electrophysiological studies, apart from
classic ﬁndings of this entity, we noticed and ﬁlmed brisk muscle leg
spasms induced by a visual cue.
Conclusions: This is the ﬁrst description of visual-induced startle
reactions in patients with SLS. This ﬁnding can shed some light on
SLS physiopathology and illustrates the importance of neurophsyio-
logical studies in patients with idiopathic increased muscle tone.
